question.problem:
Given that the random variable $X∼{χ}^{2}(4),$ calculate $P(X<9).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.

*Hint: You may wish to make use of the following result:*

$$
{\int }_{0}^{9}x{e}^{-x/2}\,\text{d}x≈3.75560
$$

*The probability density function ${χ}^{2}(k)$ is given by*

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{2}^{k/2}Γ(\frac{k}{2})}{x}^{k/2-1}{e}^{-x/2}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
A chi-square random variable $X∼{χ}^{2}(k)$ with $k$ degrees of freedom has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{2}^{k/2}Γ(\frac{k}{2})}{x}^{k/2-1}{e}^{-x/2}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $X∼{χ}^{2}(4).$ So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4Γ(2)}x{e}^{-x/2}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Recalling that $Γ(n)=(n-1)!$ for any natural number $n\ge 1,$ we have

$$
Γ(2)=1!=1.
$$

So, the probability distribution becomes

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4}x{e}^{-x/2}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate $P(X<9)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<9) & ={\int }_{0}^{9}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{9}\frac{1}{4}x{e}^{-x/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{0}^{9}x{e}^{-x/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ≈\frac{1}{4}\cdot 3.75560 \\  & =0.9389\end{aligned}
$$
